title: model-version-freeze-flow-wirecopy
body:
Purpose / context:
This is a working doc for a lightweight "freeze" (aka pin) flow that lives in the model catalog and endpoint creation paths. Goal: let engineers quickly lock an endpoint to a model binary+config with clear auditability and a migration path (staged canary, TTL lift) while avoiding surprising compatibility mismatches at deploy time. This doc focuses on wire copy, microcopy, and a prioritized grooming backlog for a first pass MVP (catalog + endpoint modal + API hook).

High-level UX idea (sketch):
- Left: model list (card/grid). Each card shows model name, version tag, size (FP16/8/quant), latency profile, last-validated commit, and a small health badge (green/yellow/red). Cards have a subtle "freeze" icon (a small padlock) that indicates whether this version is eligible to be pinned.
- Middle: selected model detail panel. Large model name, long description, risk bullets (known regressions), recent eval score changes, compatibility hints (regions/HW), suggested quantization profile. Primary actions: [Compare versions], [Freeze this version], [Recommend rollouts].
- Right: quick endpoint preview + pin controls. If user is in an endpoint creation flow show: target endpoint name, traffic split slider (for staged pin/canary), TTL for temporary pin, and an audit line showing who pinned and when (for existing pins).

Wire copy / microcopy (drafts):
- Freeze button (primary): "Freeze version" — hover tooltip: "Lock this model binary and config for this endpoint. Allows safe rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible variants."
- Freeze confirmation modal title: "Freeze model version for endpoint"
- Modal explanatory text: "Freezing binds this endpoint to the selected model binary and serving config. This prevents silent model swaps and gives you guaranteed inference reproducibility. You can schedule a staged rollout or set a temporary TTL to auto-unfreeze."
- Secondary controls in modal: checkbox: "Enable staged rollout (canary)" with tooltip: "Route X% traffic to previous version while validating outputs."
- TTL copy: "Auto-unfreeze after" placeholder: "24 hours" — helper text: "Use temporary pins for short experiments; permanent pins require org-admin approval."
- Conflict error microcopy: "This model is not available in the selected region with the chosen compute profile. Try a compatible variant or remove the pin."
- Small padlock tooltip on model cards: "Freezeable: validated for production" or "Not validated: missing perf profile"

Behavior notes / edge cases:
- If pinned model variant is unavailable in a region, endpoint creation should surface an inline banner with two CTA options: [Choose fallback] and [Request capacity].
- Pin should be reversible but with audit: unfreeze requires a reason (short text) and is logged to the endpoint audit trail. For permanent pins, require an org-admin approval flow (email or workflow).
- Support 'staged-pin' where user sets a %, duration and a regression check (optional eval prompt set). If regression check fails, auto-rollback. This ties into existing Optimize rules so we need API hooks.
- Pin compatibility check runs client-side quick validate and server-side full validate. Quick validate covers architecture, quantization compatibility, policy rules; full validate runs before commit (may take up to 30s).

Accessibility + keyboard flow:
- Freeze modal: focus trapped, first focus on heading, confirm button is last in tab order. Use role=dialog and aria-live for validation messages.
- Buttons use descriptive aria-labels: "Freeze model version v1.3.2 for endpoint 'search-api'"

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI: list->detail->freeze modal flow implemented in console (catalog and endpoint flow).
- API: POST /endpoints/:id/pins creates pin, accepts staged config (percent/duration/ttl) and returns 202 + validation status.
- Audit: every pin/unpin writes a record {user,timestamp,reason,prev_pin} visible in endpoint history.
- Errors: show clear inline messages when region/variant mismatch.
- Tests: unit + one e2e that simulates staged-pin and failed regression => auto-rollback.

Prioritized grooming backlog (initial 8 tickets):
1) PIN-UI-001: Freeze modal + microcopy (3 pts) — high
2) PIN-API-100: Pin creation endpoint + validation contract (5 pts) — high
3) PIN-AUD-010: Audit trail UI + backend events (3 pts) — medium
4) PIN-ROLL-050: Staged rollout engine integration w/Optimizer (8 pts) — high
5) PIN-UX-201: Card padlock states + tooltip copy (1 pt) — low
6) PIN-REG-300: Cheap client-side compatibility check prototype (3 pts) — medium
7) PIN-SEC-400: Admin approval workflow + RBAC guardrails (5 pts) — medium
8) PIN-E2E-900: Full e2e with TTL auto-unfreeze/rollback (5 pts) — medium

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Should we surface a global organization-level pinned model list (platform teams might want visibility across projects)? Pros: discoverability. Cons: larger surface for complexity and governance.
- Default TTL for temporary pins — 24 hours seems reasonable but needs legal/product input.
- Should pinning be allowed at model-catalog level (global) or only at endpoint-level? For MVP restrict to endpoint-level to reduce scope.
- Approval UX: email vs in-console workflow? Lean in-console for speed but add email fallback.

Metrics to track post-launch:
- % endpoints with pins vs without
- Number of auto-rollbacks triggered by staged-pin regressions
- Time-to-pin (from modal open to commit)
- Admin approval turnaround time (for permanent pins)

Next steps / owners:
- Design: Ben Carlson — finish final wireframes and hi-fi copy (2d)
- Product: Aisha Patel — finalize acceptance criteria and prioritize backlog in roadmap (this sprint)
- Eng frontend: Marisol Nguyen — spike on client-side compatibility checks (1 week)
- Eng backend: Diego Ramos — sketch API contract for pin creation and audit events (3 days)

Notes to self / meeting snippets:
- 2025-02-17 sync: Ben wants the padlock to be less prominent; Diego flagged audit schema change. Marisol suggests making staged-pin default off.
- Keep this doc iterative; copy here is the source for the copy deck linked in the PR.
